correctness.rationale: All-field proof: exactly one Frobenius-stable matching of six roots; Richelot determinant zero iff quadratic pencil and unique F_q involution; split/nonsplit involution conjugacy classes and irreducible cubic lifting yield exact masses; the explicit x^6 f(d/x)=d^3 f(x) relation and chi(d)=-1 give cancellation for every odd extension. Frobenius swaps the two elliptic eigenspace factors in nonsplit type, so polarized quotient is a quadratic Weil restriction; split type factors descend separately. The three source files are individually executable; exhaustive coefficient enumeration over p^6 monic sextics for p=3,5, exact Galois invariance, exact F_{p^2} point counting and independently exact F_{p^3} character sums establish both complete first-field spectra and odd-trace examples. Limitations and quantifiers are given in RESULT.md.

originality.rationale: The known Reis invariant-polynomial theorem completely covers the numerical involution-fixed polynomial masses, so that numerical result is not treated as new. The checked geometric Richelot literature establishes the determinant/involution test but not the precise rational elliptic-product versus quadratic-Weil-restriction dichotomy for the irreducible six-cycle locus or the full first-field Weil spectra. Direct degree-one and degree-three character checks and degree-two point-count enumeration add arithmetic information absent from the cited invariant-polynomial enumeration. Prior own genus-two matching-cycle and special decomposed-kernel studies lack the complete irreducible-sextic arithmetic quotient/Weil spectrum.

value.rationale: The original arithmetic content is a natural complete dichotomy for the codomain of a uniquely rational genus-two Richelot kernel even when Jacobian rational two-torsion is trivial: actual F_q elliptic product versus quadratic Weil restriction, with a universal all-odd-extension zero trace in the induced type. This is motivated by arithmetic isogeny computation and rational descent, not arbitrary coefficient slicing. The two first odd prime fields supply complete exact nontrivial Weil-polynomial and frequency classifications (one F_3 type, four F_5 types), not implied by the known count of invariant irreducible polynomials. The known Reis counting theorem is credited, not counted as a novelty or value source. Nontrivial classification of polarization descent plus exact finite spectra is the reason for PASS, notwithstanding simplicity of the trace involution cancellation.
